salient_findings: Slow but progressive swelling near the gluteal cleft
Mild blanching erythema of the overlying skin
Complex and septated mass in the subcutaneous tissue
key_facts: 1-year history of swelling
No fevers, chills, pain, drainage, bleeding, or rectal bleeding
4 × 4 cm area of swelling just left of the natal cleft
Mild blanching erythema of the overlying skin
No fluctuance, purulence, or visible pilonidal pits
Percutaneous aspiration was performed but no fluid was obtained
A 6-cm vertical incision was made over the lesion
A complex and septated 6 × 4 × 4 cm mass was excised
The mass was adherent to subcutaneous fat but did not involve the coccyx or anal sphincter

shortlist.label: Epidermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the description of a complex and septated mass, and is a common cause of gluteal swelling

shortlist.label: Dermoid cyst
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to epidermoid cyst, but can contain skin, hair, and other tissue, and is a plausible diagnosis given the location and characteristics of the mass

shortlist.label: Pilonidal sinus
shortlist.why_kept: Although initially considered and excluded, it remains a possible diagnosis given the location and erythema, and should be considered in the differential

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: A common cause of subcutaneous masses, and the description of the mass being adherent to subcutaneous fat is consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Desmoid tumor
shortlist.why_kept: A type of tumor that can occur in the subcutaneous tissue, and the description of the mass being complex and septated is consistent with this diagnosis

raw.rationale: The patient presented with a 1-year history of progressive swelling near the gluteal cleft, and a complex and septated mass was excised from the subcutaneous tissue, which is consistent with an epidermoid cyst. The absence of fluid or purulence on aspiration and the solid, multiloculated nature of the mass also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Pilonidal sinus
rejected.why: No evidence of pilonidal pits or fluctuance

rejected.label: Lipoma
rejected.why: The mass was complex and septated, not typical of a lipoma

rejected.label: Desmoid tumor
rejected.why: The mass did not involve the coccyx or anal sphincter and was not described as aggressive or infiltrative

rejected.label: Dermoid cyst
rejected.why: The location and description of the mass are more consistent with an epidermoid cyst
